ok-40027-bos-matter-3775.title:
Discussion and possible action regarding - Presentation of Proclamations by Senator Lisa Standridge and the Cleveland County Commissioners to the Sons of the American Revolution in appreciation for their efforts in the creation and installation of the America250 commemorative bench.   

Senator Lisa Stanford (Cleveland County)
Presentation of State Senate Citations

Senator Lisa Stanford addressed the Senate to present two official Citations of Appreciation honoring individuals who contributed to the historic preservation and community pride of Cleveland County.

1. Citation of Appreciation: Ralph L. Stevenson Jr.
Senator Stanford read and presented a citation to Ralph L. Stevenson Jr. for his leadership during the United States Semiquincentennial (250th anniversary) commemoration.

Key Achievements Noted: 
Served as Chairman of the 250 Memorial Bench Committee; successfully led fundraising, design, and installation efforts for the Leonard Monroe Bench at the Cleveland County Courthouse; designed the Oklahoma SAR 250 commemorative pin.

Pursuant to a formal motion, the Oklahoma State Legislature extended its official congratulations and directed the citation to be formally presented to Mr. Stevenson.

2. Citation of Appreciation: Tony Eastman
Senator Stanford read and presented a citation to Tony Eastman, President of the Norman Chapter of the Sons of the American Revolution (SAR).

Key Achievements Noted: 
Approved and championed the 250 Memorial Bench project; integrated the project into the broader National SAR Society and Oklahoma SAR goals; organized a dedication ceremony attended by nearly 100 community members.

Pursuant to a formal motion, the Oklahoma State Legislature extended its official congratulations and directed the citation to be formally presented to Mr. Eastman.

Closing Remarks Senator Stanford noted for the record that the newly dedicated 250 Memorial Bench is permanently located on the southeast corner of the Cleveland County Courthouse grounds. A brief recess was taken following the presentations for official photographs with the honorees.

Following the Senate presentations, Alyse Moore presented two official Proclamations on behalf of the Board of County Commissioners and the People of Cleveland County to further honor the community contributions of Mr. Stevenson and Mr. Eastman.

Proclamation for Ralph L. Stevenson, Jr.

Key Points Noted: Recognized his dedicated service as the Chairman of the 250th Memorial Bench Committee and his work with the Sons of the American Revolution (SAR) to promote patriotism and preserve history. Special appreciation was given to his creative talents in designing the local Memorial Bench and the Oklahoma SAR 250 commemorative pin.

The Board of County Commissioners and the citizens of Cleveland County formally extended their gratitude to Mr. Stevenson for preserving their shared history.

Proclamation for Tony Eastman

Key Points Noted: Recognized his leadership as the Norman Chapter President of the Sons of the American Revolution (SAR). The proclamation highlighted his leadership in spearheading the community effort to place the permanent America 250 Memorial Bench on the Cleveland County Courthouse grounds.

The Board of County Commissioners and the citizens of Cleveland County formally extended their gratitude to Mr. Eastman for his civic service and dedication to historical remembrance.

ok-40027-bos-matter-3809.title:
Discussion and possible action regarding a Resolution to approve the Appointment of HUB International as Insurance Broker of Record for Employee Health, Dental, and Vision Benefits, effective September 14, 2026.

Caitlin Hinman, Senior VP, from HUB International presented a request to the Board regarding the county's insurance coverage's.

Ms. Hinman highlighted the firm's long-standing partnership with the county as the current Broker of Record for workers' compensation, noting their ongoing success in premium negotiations, claims advocacy, and return-to-work programs.

In light of the projected 2027 rate increases and reduced coverage under the current HealthChoice program, Ms. Hinman presented a financial analysis exploring a transition to Blue Cross Blue Shield. This marks the third evaluation conducted by HUB International to help the county gain greater control over its health insurance program.

Ms. Hinman formally requested that the Board approve HUB International as the Broker of Record for health insurance, contingent upon the county's decision to exit the HealthChoice program. This appointment would allow HUB International to manage the medical coverage line in the same capacity as the workers' compensation coverage.
